target_customer: Pregnant parents who want to bank cord blood, cord tissue and placenta stem cells
problem: Cord blood banking was costly and opaque. Anja offers a more transparent, doctor backed and cheaper service.
business_model: Direct to consumer collection kit plus annual storage fees, with lab partner Vitalant
product_category: Cord blood and tissue banking, consumer health

founders.name: Kathryn Cross
education: Wellesley College, BA Media Arts and Sciences and Economics
founders.background_notes: Founded the company in memory of her brother Andrew who had cerebral palsy. Built a pregnancy and cord blood community on TikTok as @kathrynanja.

competitors.name: Cord Blood Registry
competitors.what: Largest US private cord blood bank, owned by CooperSurgical
competitors.traction_then: One of three firms holding most US market share

competitors.name: ViaCord
competitors.what: Private cord blood and tissue bank
competitors.traction_then: One of three firms holding most US market share

competitors.name: Cryo-Cell
competitors.what: Public company offering cord blood and tissue banking
competitors.traction_then: One of three firms holding most US market share

technical_complexity.rationale: Logistics and kit shipping around an existing accredited lab partner, with little original technology.

defensibility.rationale: Customers store samples for years so churn is low once enrolled, but new customer acquisition was marketing driven and large incumbents held scale.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents did not copy it in sources found. YC lists the company as acquired but no acquirer was found.

market_need_then: Incumbent prices were high, for example first year fees of about 2,470 to 2,625 dollars for Cryo-Cell and CBR on a competitor's page, leaving room for a cheaper, transparent brand.

branding.domain_note: Uses anjahealth.com with a Health suffix.

identity.voice_and_tone: Warm and reassuring, transparent, peace of mind, contrasts itself with average cord blood banks

branding.brand_signature: Founder led TikTok community and the story of honoring her brother Andrew
branding.community_and_virality: Founder built a pregnancy and cord blood banking community on TikTok per the YC page. Brand listed on a product review site, Thingtesting.

brand_strength.rationale: Clear warm voice and a founder story with an audience, but no independent press about the brand itself found.

outcome_analysis: Anja raised a 4.5 million dollar seed in May 2022 led by Seven Seven Six and sold a cheaper, more transparent cord blood service using founder TikTok reach. YC marks it acquired, but no acquirer or date is public, the site is still live in 2026 and a new CEO was named in June 2026, so the structure of the outcome is unclear.
notes: Exit type follows the YC directory status Acquired, but no buyer, date or price was found, and a June 2026 press release announces Jan Chen as CEO with Kathryn Cross still called founder, so the acquisition may be partial or unreported. A single source mentions a 2 million dollar seed in May 2024 with YC and others, unverified and excluded. Totals of 4.62M and 5.25M appear on aggregators. Headquarters is given as Los Angeles or San Jose. Competitors are cited from a 2020 market report listing the three largest US banks, no traction numbers given. Name origin not found.
